Los bloques anteriores enseñan; este ord: The previous blocks teach; this one organises. There are no new formulas here: there is a map of what the university entrance exam covers, a catalogue of the mistakes that cost the most marks, a formula sheet generated by itself from the topics and two timed mock papers. It is worth going through it twice: at the start of the year, to see the ground, and in the last weeks, to decide what to revise.
Este bloque no enseña nada nuevo: ordena: This block teaches nothing new: it organises what you have already seen. Getting to the university entrance exam depends not so much on having studied a lot as on knowing what is covered, how you stand in each part and what each topic needs in order to be understood. That is what the map below gathers.
En 2.º de Bachillerato hay dos asignatur: In the final year of Spanish upper secondary there are two mathematics subjects with exams of their own. Matemáticas II, on the science and technology track, puts the weight on matrix algebra, the geometry of space and full analysis, with integrals. Mathematics Applied to the Social Sciences II shares with it matrices, systems, derivatives and probability, but swaps the geometry of space for linear programming and adds statistical inference: estimating and testing from a sample.
Cada comunidad autónoma redacta su propi: Each autonomous community writes its own exam, and the formats change from year to year: number of questions, choice of parts, marks for each section. The syllabus in the map is the common one of the national curriculum; before the last weeks, look up your university's papers from earlier years and compare them with it.
Elige la asignatura. Cada tema aparece c: Choose the subject. Each topic appears with your state —“not started”, “seen” or “mastered”— and with the topics it takes for granted. If one gets stuck, the last column says where to start pulling the thread: it is almost never the topic itself that fails, but something it assumes.
<strong>Primero el mapa, después los tem: The map first, the topics after. Start with the topics that have most topics behind them: matrices hold up determinants, the inverse and the discussion of systems; derivatives hold up sketching, optimisation and integrals.
<strong>Repasar es resolver, no releer.<: Revising is solving, not rereading. Rereading gives the feeling that everything is clear. Solving an exercise without looking at the theory is the only thing that tells you whether you know it. Use each topic's exercises with “Another” until they come out first time.
<strong>Espacia el repaso.</strong> La p: Space out your revision. The home page remembers what you get wrong and offers it again after one, three and seven days, under “To revise today”. Coming back to a topic once you have started to forget it fixes it far better than hammering away at it the same day.
<strong>Haz simulacros con reloj.</stron: Do timed mock papers. An exam does not only measure what you know: it measures whether you can do it in ninety minutes and without hints. The mock papers in this block draw questions from the topics and tell you at the end what to revise.
<strong>Estudia tus errores, no solo los: Study your mistakes, not only your right answers. The topic on the mistakes that cost the most marks collects the usual ones. Recognising them in somebody else's exam is the first step towards not making them in yours.
Te quedan tres tardes y fallas la discus: You have three afternoons left and you keep getting the discussion of systems with a parameter wrong. Where do you start?
Por la discusión de sistemas, que es lo: With the discussion of systems, which is what comes up in the exam
Si falla la base, machacar el tema de ar: If the foundation fails, hammering away at the topic above fixes nothing. The discussion takes rank and determinants for granted; if those fail, the discussion will keep failing.
Por lo que da por sabido: rango y determ: With what it takes for granted: rank and determinants
Es lo que dice la última columna del map: That is what the last column of the map says. An afternoon of rank exercises usually unblocks the whole discussion; then an afternoon of discussion with a parameter and the third for a mock paper.
Por releer la teoría de los tres temas: By rereading the theory of the three topics
Releer da sensación de dominio sin compr: Rereading gives a feeling of mastery without checking it. Solving exercises with “Another” until they come out first time is the only thing that tells you whether you know it.
Releer produce la sensación de saber; so: Rereading produces the feeling of knowing; only solving without looking at the theory checks it. If a topic “is understood” but its exercises fail, it has not been learned.
Empezar por el tema que más gusta: Starting with the topic you like best
Suele ser el que ya se sabe. El tiempo r: It is usually the one you already know. Time pays off better on the topic with most topics hanging off it and the worst state.
Dejar los simulacros para el final: Leaving the mock papers until the end
El primer simulacro dice dónde estás; si: The first mock paper says where you are; without it, revision runs blind. One at the start, another halfway and another at the end.
El examen mide también velocidad. Un eje: The exam also measures speed. An exercise that takes twenty minutes is no use if the paper allows ten.
Planificar un repaso es un problema de d: Planning revision is a dependency problem, just like planning building work or compiling a program: you cannot put the roof on before the walls. The column “What it takes for granted” is a [[av-grafos|directed graph]] of topics, and the sensible order for studying them is a topological sort of that graph, the same one a package manager uses to install the dependencies before the program that needs them.
Matemáticas II y MACS II comparten matri: Matemáticas II and MACS II share matrices, systems, derivatives and probability; the first adds the geometry of space and integrals, the second linear programming and inference.
Cuando un tema se atasca, suele fallar a: When a topic gets stuck, something it takes for granted is usually failing: look at its prerequisites.
Repasar es resolver sin mirar, con el re: Revising is solving without looking, with spaced repetition and timed mock papers.
